name: OpenAI-compatible API
description: Use a familiar API format with your configured REACH or compatible endpoint.
detail: Configure the base URL, access key if required, and a model exposed by your host. The website does not test or connect to endpoints.

name: VS Code
description: Keep chat and coding alongside your project files in the REACH extension.
detail: The repository includes the VS Code extension source and setup guide. Use the documented installation path for your environment.

name: SimpleRAG
description: Host and manage the relay through the integrated REACH control panel.
detail: The SimpleRAG plugin adds Dashboard, Browser, Endpoint, Models, Usage, Logs, Settings, and About pages. Follow the project README for setup.

name: REACH Studio
description: A standalone home for files, conversations, personas, and agent teams.
detail: Run Studio on macOS, Windows, or Linux. Configure a compatible endpoint inside Settings → Connection & default model.

name: ChatGPT bridge
description: A provider option in the existing REACH desktop tray and editor UI.
detail: Requires the corresponding signed-in provider session and local bridge configuration. Provider terms, access requirements, and limits apply.

name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
description: Connect through the Copilot option in the local desktop bridge.
detail: Requires the matching provider account and session. Follow the project’s tray setup guide; this is not a Microsoft endorsement.

name: Gemini web
description: A web-provider route available through the project’s local bridge UI.
detail: Requires an eligible provider session and the local bridge. Availability and usage are governed by the provider.

name: CodeGPT
description: The existing UI includes a CodeGPT economy-model provider option.
detail: This route depends on the host’s CodeGPT setup and available model catalog. Provider subscriptions and model access rules still apply.

name: REACH relay
description: Connect compatible clients to the endpoint managed by your host.
detail: Host-managed API keys and the configured model catalog determine access. Use the local or hosted URL supplied by the operator.
